items.prompt: In this food chain, what does the caterpillar eat?

figure.alt: Food chain: leaf, arrow, caterpillar, arrow, bird.

options.why: The arrow goes from the caterpillar to the bird, so the bird eats the caterpillar.
The chain shows the caterpillar eating something else.
Every animal must eat. The arrow shows what it eats.

hints: Arrows point from the food to the eater.
Find the arrow that points to the caterpillar.
Where does that arrow start?
items.explanation: The arrow points from the leaf to the caterpillar. This means the caterpillar eats the leaf.

items.prompt: Every food chain starts with a green plant. A plant is called a ___ because it makes its own food.
hints: Plants make their own food.
Animals that eat are called consumers.
The word starts with p.
items.explanation: Plants are producers because they make their own food using light. Every food chain begins with a producer.

items.prompt: Put this rice field food chain in order, starting with the producer.
hints: The producer is the plant.
What eats rice plants in a field?
Which animal hunts the snake?
items.explanation: Rats eat rice plants, snakes eat rats and eagles eat snakes. So the chain is rice plant, rat, snake, eagle.

items.prompt: What does an arrow in a food chain show?

options.why: Arrows have nothing to do with size.

options.text: the direction the food and energy go
which animals live next to each other
options.why: Arrows do not show where animals live.

options.text: which way the animal is facing
options.why: Arrows do not show which way an animal faces.

hints: An arrow points from one living thing to another.
It points from the food to the eater.
What moves along the chain when one thing eats another?
items.explanation: An arrow points from the food to the eater. It shows food and energy passing along the chain.

items.prompt: Look at this food chain. Which animal is both a predator and prey?

figure.alt: Food chain: seeds, arrow, mouse, arrow, snake, arrow, owl.

options.why: Nothing eats the owl in this chain. It is the top predator.
The mouse is prey, but it does not hunt animals here.
Seeds come from a plant. They are the producer.

hints: A predator hunts other animals.
Prey is hunted by another animal.
Find an animal that eats an animal and is eaten too.
items.explanation: The snake hunts the mouse, so it is a predator. The owl eats the snake, so the snake is also prey.

items.prompt: Match each word to its meaning.
pairs: makes its own food using light
gets energy by eating other living things
an animal that is hunted and eaten
hints: Two words are about how a living thing gets food.
Two words are about hunting.
Start with producer. What does a plant make?
items.explanation: Producers make food using light and consumers eat other living things. Predators hunt prey, and prey are the animals that get eaten.

items.prompt: Look at the food chain grass → rabbit → fox. What happens first if all the foxes disappear?

options.text: The number of rabbits goes down.
options.why: Foxes eat rabbits. With no foxes, fewer rabbits are eaten.
Grass would be eaten more over time, but not all at once.
Removing one living thing affects the others in its chain.

options.text: The number of rabbits goes up.

hints: Foxes eat rabbits.
Think about what stops eating the rabbits.
Would more or fewer rabbits survive?
items.explanation: With no foxes, fewer rabbits get eaten, so their numbers go up. Later, more rabbits would eat more grass.

items.prompt: Choose 2 producers.

options.why: Goats eat plants. They are consumers.
Mushrooms cannot make food from light, so they are not producers.
Frogs eat insects. They are consumers.

hints: Producers make their own food using light.
Producers are usually green.
Check each one: could it make food in sunlight?
items.explanation: Mango trees and seaweed use light to make food, so they are producers. Mushrooms, goats and frogs must get food from other living things.

items.prompt: Where does the energy in every food chain first come from?

options.why: Soil gives plants water and minerals. The energy comes from sunlight.
The top predator is at the end of the chain, not the start.
Living things need water, but it does not give them energy.

hints: Every food chain starts with a plant.
Plants need something to make their food.
What do leaves catch?
items.explanation: Plants use energy from sunlight to make food. That energy passes along the chain when animals eat.

items.prompt: How many consumers are in this food chain?

figure.alt: Food chain: pond weed, arrow, tadpole, arrow, fish, arrow, heron.

hints: Consumers eat other living things.
The pond weed is a producer.
Count every living thing after the pond weed.
items.explanation: The tadpole, fish and heron all eat other living things, so there are 3 consumers. The pond weed is the producer.

items.prompt: In a rice field, snakes eat rats and rats eat rice. People catch all the snakes. What happens to the rice?

options.text: The rice grows better, because snakes ate rice.
options.why: Snakes do not eat rice. They eat rats.

options.text: More rice is eaten, because there are more rats.

options.why: Removing snakes changes the number of rats, which affects the rice.

options.text: All the rats leave the field.
options.why: With no snakes, rats are safer, so they stay.

hints: Snakes eat rats.
Without snakes, what happens to the number of rats?
What do rats eat?
items.explanation: With no snakes, more rats survive. More rats eat more rice, so farmers lose more of their crop.

items.prompt: The table shows what each animal eats. If all the grasshoppers die, which animal loses food first?

head: Animal
Eats
figure.alt: Table of what animals eat: grasshopper eats grass, rabbit eats grass, frog eats grasshoppers, snake eats frogs and rabbits, eagle eats snakes.

options.why: Rabbits eat grass, not grasshoppers.
Eagles eat snakes. They may be affected later, not first.
Snakes eat frogs and rabbits. They are affected later.

hints: Find the animals that eat grasshoppers.
Read the Eats column.
Which animal eats only grasshoppers?
items.explanation: Frogs eat grasshoppers, so they lose their food first. Snakes might be affected later, but they can still eat rabbits.

items.prompt: Draw a food chain with a producer and three consumers. Draw the arrows the right way.

criteria.label: Arrows point from the food to the eater
Labels the producer and the consumers

hints: Start with a green plant.
Each arrow means is eaten by.
items.explanation: A food chain starts with a plant. Each arrow points from the living thing that is eaten to the one that eats it.

items.prompt: Which of these is a consumer?

options.why: Grass makes its own food, so it is a producer.
A tree makes its own food, so it is a producer.
Seaweed makes its own food, so it is a producer.

hints: A consumer cannot make its own food.
A consumer has to eat something.
Look for the animal.
items.explanation: A rabbit eats plants, so it is a consumer. The others are plants that make their own food.

items.prompt: Label the food chain. One label is not needed.

figure.alt: A food chain with three pictures joined by arrows pointing to the right: grass, then a mouse, then an owl.

hints: The first living thing is a plant.
The mouse is hunted by the owl.
The owl hunts the mouse.
items.explanation: Grass is the producer. The mouse is eaten by the owl, so it is prey. The owl hunts, so it is the predator.

items.prompt: Tap the animal that is a predator and also prey.

figure.alt: A food chain with four pictures joined by arrows pointing to the right: a leaf, a caterpillar, a frog and a snake.

hints: It eats something and is eaten by something.
The first animal in the chain only gets eaten.
The last animal in the chain is not eaten.
items.explanation: The frog eats the caterpillar, so it is a predator, and the snake eats the frog, so it is also prey.

items.prompt: Complete the table for the food chain grass, rabbit, fox.
items.caption: Grass, rabbit, fox
head: Living thing
Eats
Eaten by
hints: The arrow points to the animal that does the eating.
The rabbit eats the grass.
The fox eats the rabbit.
items.explanation: The rabbit eats grass and the fox eats the rabbit. Grass is eaten by the rabbit.

items.prompt: The table shows animals on a farm over three years. What do the numbers suggest?

head: Year
Foxes
Rabbits
figure.alt: Table of animals on a farm. Year 1: 4 foxes and 60 rabbits. Year 2: 8 foxes and 35 rabbits. Year 3: 12 foxes and 18 rabbits.

options.text: More foxes eat more rabbits, so rabbit numbers fall
Rabbits eat foxes, so fox numbers rise
options.why: Foxes hunt rabbits. Rabbits do not eat foxes.

options.text: More rabbits are born when foxes arrive
options.why: The rabbit numbers fall, so more are not being born.

options.text: Foxes and rabbits are not connected
options.why: The numbers change together, which shows they are connected.

hints: Compare how the two columns change.
One number goes up and the other goes down.
Think about what foxes eat.
items.explanation: The foxes go up from 4 to 12 while the rabbits fall from 60 to 18. This fits predators eating prey.

items.prompt: A food chain has 5 living things. How many arrows does it have?
hints: Draw 5 dots in a row.
An arrow joins one dot to the next.
Count the gaps between the dots.
items.explanation: There is one arrow between each pair of neighbours, so 5 living things have 4 arrows.

items.prompt: Sort each animal by what it eats.
hints: Herbivores eat only plants.
Carnivores eat only animals.
Omnivores eat both plants and animals.
items.explanation: Cows and rabbits eat plants, lions and snakes eat animals, and chickens and bears eat both.

items.prompt: Put this pond food chain in order, starting with the producer.
hints: Start with the living thing that makes its own food.
Tadpoles eat algae.
The heron is at the end.
items.explanation: Algae make food, tadpoles eat the algae, fish eat the tadpoles and the heron eats the fish.

items.prompt: A farmer sprays a field and kills all the insects. Which animals are affected first?

options.text: plants that grow in the field
options.why: Plants make their own food and do not eat insects.
The sun does not eat anything.
Soil is not a living thing that eats insects.

hints: Find the animals that eat insects.
A food chain shows who eats whom.
The animals that eat insects lose their food.
items.explanation: Birds that eat insects lose their food first. Their numbers may fall.

items.prompt: Rangga says, "A plant is a producer because it takes food from the soil." What is the correct reason?

options.text: It takes in food from other plants
options.why: A plant does not eat other plants.
Plants do not eat animals.
Colour is not the reason. It is what the plant does.

options.text: It makes its own food using light, water and air

hints: A producer makes its own food.
Plants use sunlight to make food in their leaves.
Soil gives plants water and minerals, not food.
items.explanation: A plant makes its own food in its leaves using light, water and air. That is why it is a producer.

items.prompt: Look at the chain algae, shrimp, fish, seal. Choose 2 true sentences.

options.text: The algae make their own food

options.why: Shrimp eat algae. They cannot make their own food.

options.text: Nothing in this chain eats the fish
options.why: The seal eats the fish.

hints: Producers make their own food.
A predator hunts other animals.
Follow the arrows to see who eats whom.
items.explanation: Algae are producers, and the seal hunts the fish so it is a predator.

items.prompt: Look at the table. All the lizards die. Which is most likely to happen?

figure.caption: Who eats what
head: Animal
What it eats
figure.alt: Table of who eats what. Grasshopper eats grass. Lizard eats grasshoppers. Mouse eats grass. Snake eats lizards and mice.

options.text: Snakes die out because they have no food
options.why: Snakes also eat mice, so they still have food.

options.text: Grasshoppers decrease because lizards are gone
options.why: Lizards eat grasshoppers, so fewer lizards means fewer grasshoppers eaten.

options.text: Grasshoppers increase and snakes still have mice to eat

options.why: Mice eat grass and are not affected by the lizards dying.

hints: Find who eats the lizards and what lizards eat.
Fewer lizards means fewer grasshoppers are eaten.
Check whether the snake has another food.
items.explanation: Fewer lizards means more grasshoppers survive. Snakes still eat mice, so they survive.

items.prompt: An animal that is hunted for food is called ___.
hints: The hunter is the predator.
This is the animal that gets eaten.
It starts with the letter p.
items.explanation: The hunted animal is the prey.

items.prompt: A ___ makes its own food. A ___ must eat other living things.
hints: Plants make food in their leaves.
Animals have to find food.
Use the words producer and consumer.
items.explanation: Plants are producers. Animals are consumers because they eat other living things.

items.prompt: Look at the chart of a field food chain. Why are there so few hawks?

figure.alt: Bar chart of living things in a field. Grass plants 200, caterpillars 40, small birds 8, hawk 1.

options.why: Hawks are predators and eat other animals.

options.text: Each hawk needs to eat many small birds
Hawks are the only living things that make food
options.why: Plants make food. Hawks cannot.

options.text: Hawks are too small to count
options.why: Hawks are big. Their numbers are small because they need a lot of food.

hints: Look at how the bars get shorter along the chain.
Each animal eats many of the one before it.
Think about how much food one hawk needs.
items.explanation: Each animal needs to eat many of the living things before it, so the numbers get smaller towards the end of the chain.

items.prompt: True or false: A food chain always starts with a plant.
hints: Which living things make their own food?
What gets eaten first?
Plants are at the start.
items.explanation: Plants make their own food using light, so they are the first link. Animals then eat plants or each other.

items.prompt: True or false: In a food chain, an arrow points from the animal to the thing that it eats.
hints: What is the arrow showing?
Does energy go to the eater?
Arrows point to the eater.
items.explanation: Arrows show the way energy goes, so they point from the food to the animal that eats it. In grass, then rabbit, the arrow goes from grass to rabbit.

items.prompt: True or false: A predator is an animal that hunts and eats other animals.
hints: What do we call the hunted animal?
Hunters are predators.
Predators hunt prey.
items.explanation: A hawk is a predator and the mouse it hunts is its prey.

items.prompt: True or false: A rabbit that eats grass is a producer.
hints: Does a rabbit make its own food?
Who eats the grass?
Rabbits are consumers.
items.explanation: Producers make their own food, like grass. A rabbit eats grass, so it is a consumer, specifically a herbivore.

items.prompt: An animal that hunts other animals is a ___.
hints: The animal it hunts is the prey.
A lion is one.
It starts with pred.
items.explanation: A predator hunts and eats other animals, called prey.
